stories.title: Russia opens first road bridge with North Korea
stories.summary: Russia and North Korea have opened their first road bridge across the Tumen River as political, economic and military ties between the two countries deepen.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5M4bT The new Russia-North Korea road bridge is named after Soviet Red Army officer Yakov Novichenko, who is credited with saving North Korean founder Kim Il Sung's life Image: Yuri Smityuk/TASS/picture alliance Advertisement Russia and North Korea on Monday cut the ribbon on the first road bridge linking the two countries as Moscow and Pyongyang deepen their strategic partnership. The crossing spans the Tumen River and marks another expansion of transport links between the two countries. Where is the new bridge? The road crossing is near the existing Friendship Bridge, a railway bridge commissioned in 1959 following the Korean War. Russia and North Korea already have direct rail and air connections, but until now there had been no road bridge between them. The new bridge is named after Soviet Red Army officer Yakov Novichenko, who is credited with saving North Korean founder Kim Il Sung's life. Relatives of Novichenko attended the opening ceremony. Hungary's new prime minister, Peter Magyar, and his Tisza party want to retrieve funds and assets that went — in some dubious ways — to the family of ousted Hungarian leader Viktor Orban or his allies, various oligarchs, or frontmen.
